elements_selected.content:
Rewrite src/search.rs to query Tantivy instead of grep-scanning files. This is the core replacement per ADR-013-001.

Updated SearchMatch struct (SPEC-013 §4.7):
  pub struct SearchMatch {
      pub page: String,
      pub path: String,
      pub line: u32,
      pub column: u32,
      pub context: Option<String>,
      pub heading: Option<String>,      // NEW: enclosing heading text
      pub heading_level: Option<u8>,    // NEW: heading depth (1-6)
      pub score: f64,                   // NEW: BM25 score
  }

Updated SearchOutput struct:
  pub struct SearchOutput {
      pub query: String,
      pub total_matches: usize,
      pub results: Vec<SearchMatch>,
      // near/depth/neighbourhood_size added in Phase 2
  }

Remove: SearchConfig.regex field, SearchConfig.body_only field (always body-only now), build_matcher(), Matcher enum, the entire grep-based find_matches_in_content().

Query flow (SPEC-013 §4.4):
  1. Open or lazily build the Tantivy index.
  2. Parse query with QueryParser against body field.
  3. Execute with TopDocs collector, limited to --limit.
  4. For each matched document:
     a. Read the original file from disk.
     b. Compute body_text_ranges.
     c. Scan body text for query term occurrences (case-insensitive by default, case-sensitive with --case-sensitive). Find line/column for each occurrence.
     d. Detect headings via detect_headings().
     e. Attach heading context via find_heading_for_offset().
     f. Emit SearchMatch entries with the document's BM25 score.
  5. Order results by descending score, ties broken by path (ascending) then line (ascending).

The re-scanning step (4b-c) is necessary because Tantivy provides document-level scores but not character offsets. Split the query string on whitespace to get individual terms for re-scanning.

Retain: --case-sensitive flag (for re-scan), --path filter (applied to Tantivy results), --context chars, --limit.
Remove: --regex flag, --all flag.

REQ-013-002, REQ-013-005, CON-013-001.
